title: Building an LLM Knowledge Base
blurb: Treat your wiki like a compiler: raw sources are source code, the LLM is the compiler, the wiki is the executable, linting finds gaps, and queries run against it. Every question you ask compounds the base.
body:
The mental model that makes everything click: think of your knowledge base like a compiler pipeline.

The five stages

  • Source code = your raw/ folder — articles, papers, repos, bookmarks (never edited directly).
  • Compiler = the LLM — summarizes, links, and structures the knowledge.
  • Executable = the wiki/ — compiled articles with backlinks, encyclopedia-style.
  • Test suite = linting — find gaps, stale data, broken links.
  • Runtime = queries — Q&A against the wiki, and answers file themselves back in.

The compounding loop

Ask a question → LLM synthesizes across articles → file the answer as a new entry → the wiki grows → future answers get better. Knowledge compounds — each cycle makes the base richer.

A neat scale insight: at roughly ~400K words, an entire wiki fits in context — so you may not even need RAG. Linting keeps it healthy; outputs compound back in.

SOURCE · "Building an LLM Knowledge Base," Karpathy-style architecture diagram. This is the blueprint the AI Feed itself is built on.
